title: What is known about 1RB0RA_1RC1RD_1LD1LB_0RF1LE_1LE0LC_---1RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RA_1RC1RD_1LD1LB_0RF1LE_1LE0LC_---1RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The head sweeps the whole tape. To the left the tape is long domains of 01 (written 0111 after a rightward sweep), separated by the defect 1010 111; to the right a long period-10 comb, then a short periodic tail. The leftward sweeps over all of these are proved shift rules; how the domains and the comb change has not been found. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide, and proves the shift rules of the sweeps (lean/Rules.lean); the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 38,776 cells have been visited and 26,463 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.583). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.301).

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: The leftward sweeps: L (0111)^n E>1 R (each 0111 becomes 1010), L (01)^n E>1 R and L (10)^n C>1 R (the pairs change phase), and L (0100110111)^n E>0 R over the period-10 comb, for every n and all tapes L, R.

claims.title: Domains of 01 and a comb
claims.text: At step 142,116,130 (width 14,728, left end) the tape is (01)^103, (01)^4480, (01)^342, (01)^1050, (01)^120, (01)^52 separated by (10)^4 111, then the comb (1010111010)^221 and a tail ((01)^6 (10)^4 111)^k. At step 1,041,927,495 the comb has 891 copies and the domains are 3312, 168, 11072, 176, 50. Seen at the end turns of the run; not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts on F0, reached as D>0 0 (D reads 0, moves right onto a 0). The sweeps never produce it inside a domain or the comb; whether a defect or the tail ever does is open.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The left side of the tape is long runs of 01, the right side a regular comb with a period of ten cells. The head crosses both by proved rules, but the lengths of the runs change irregularly.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 38,776 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).
The comb on the right of the tape, 891 copies at step 10<sup>9</sup>.

sections.heading: Domains of 01, then a comb
html: The left part is domains of the pairs 01, separated by short defects (10)^4 111; after a rightward sweep a domain reads (0111)^m. The right part is a comb of period 10 and a short tail. Two end turns:
The leftward sweeps over all three backgrounds are proved shift rules (lean/Rules.lean).

sections.heading: Uneven domains
html: The domains of 01 are few and very uneven (4480 next to 52 above; at step 1,041,927,495 they are 3312, 168, 11072, 176, 50 and the comb has 891 copies). The tail is a repetition of (01)^6 (10)^4 111. No rule for the change of the domain lengths has been found.

sections.heading: One pattern
html: F0 is the only halting transition, reached as D>0 0. It cannot happen inside a domain or the comb; whether a defect or the tail ever produces it is open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.583). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.301).
After 109 steps the tape spans 38,776 cells (27,339 left of the start, 2,108 right), with a density of 1s of 0.682.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A bouncer whose left part is long domains of the pairs 01 separated by the defect 1010 111, and whose right part is a period-10 comb ending in a periodic tail; the domain lengths and the comb change from sweep to sweep with no known rule.
family: bouncer with 01 domains and a period-10 comb
